items.title: Gaja Capital is raising funds through an IPO primarily to meet its own sponsor commitments in its AIF structures, including offshore vehicles. A key q...
items.description_html:
Gaja Capital is raising funds through an IPO primarily to meet its own sponsor commitments in its AIF structures, including offshore vehicles.

A key question is — if the existing sponsor capital has already increased by nearly 20% in the last year, why does the company need to raise fresh capital from public investors to invest further in these high-risk, illiquid assets?

Interestingly, around 85% of Gaja’s income comes from management fees and carried interest, while income from sponsor commitments contributes only about 10%.

This raises a fundamental question: a significant portion of the fresh issue proceeds is being deployed toward an activity that currently contributes a relatively small share of revenue.

Moreover, carried interest is dependent on successful exits and realisation of investment gains. Until portfolio investments are monetised, the carried interest recorded in financial statements may not necessarily translate into actual cash inflows.

The key investor question is whether the additional sponsor commitments will create enough incremental value through future fee income and carry generation to justify the capital being raised

items.title: 🚨 C2C’s auditor has issued a qualified opinion and flagged multiple serious financial and compliance concerns: 1️⃣ Liquidity & Going Concern Ris...
items.description_html:
🚨 C2C’s auditor has issued a qualified opinion and flagged multiple serious financial and compliance concerns:

1️⃣ Liquidity & Going Concern Risk:
The company is facing a liquidity crisis, with statutory dues unpaid due to lack of funds. Recovery from trade receivables remains uncertain, while operations are heavily dependent on short-term promoter funding. The auditor has raised doubt over C2C’s ability to continue as a going concern. Liquidation Risk

2️⃣ CSR Payments Not Cleared:
CSR expenses were recognised through cheques, creating a book overdraft. However, the cheques were not presented for payment. The auditor noted that the CSR obligation is discharged only when the payment is actually cleared.

3️⃣ Statutory Dues Pending:
Undisputed statutory payments remain unpaid. No provision has been made for possible interest or penalties. Delays in filing statutory returns and weak internal controls were also highlighted.

4️⃣ Labour Code Impact Not Assessed:
The company has not quantified the potential impact of new labour regulations on gratuity, provident fund, wages and other employee benefits.

5️⃣ FEMA Compliance Issues:
Overseas receivables remain unrealised beyond RBI timelines. Applications for regularisation are pending, SOFTEX registration is yet to be approved, and possible penalties have not been provided for.

items.title: Pine Labs - Moving From Payments to a Full Stack Commerce OS Detailed Insights from Annual Report FY26 It is essentially trying to become the underlyi...
items.description_html:
Pine Labs - Moving From Payments to a Full Stack Commerce OS

Detailed Insights from Annual Report FY26

It is essentially trying to become the underlying technology platform that powers the entire commerce journey, not just the payment transaction.

Pine Labs should no longer be viewed simply as a POS/payment acceptance business.

The business is gradually moving from "winning the payment transaction" to monetising everything around that transaction - acceptance, processing, affordability, issuing, prepaid, loyalty, data, underwriting, merchant software & eventually AI led commerce.

Management describes the architecture as four layers - payment rails at the bottom, processing infrastructure, orchestration & financial platforms at the top.

The lower layers are particularly sticky because Pine Labs has become deeply integrated into bank settlement systems, merchant ERP/billing systems & payment workflows, making replacement closer to a system migration than simply changing a payment vendor.

FY26 Platform GTV increased 50% YoY to $194 Bn & transactions grew 30% to more than 740 Cr. Digital checkout points increased 14% to 20.3 lakh & merchants grew 16% to more than 11 lakh.

REV grew 19% to 2,711 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA increased 57% to 559 Cr with margins expanding to 21%. PAT turned positive at 113 Cr versus a loss of 145 Cr in FY25, while operating cash flow increased 8x to 395 Cr.

REV has compounded at 19% over the last 3 years, but adjusted EBITDA has compounded at 42%, while margins have moved from 9% in FY24 to 21% in FY26.

Pine Labs has spent years building distribution, technology infrastructure, regulatory licences & integrations. It is now entering what management calls the "monetisation at scale" phase.

The moat is increasingly the network rather than the payment device itself.

Pine Labs now sits between more than 11 lakh merchants, 750+ consumer brands & enterprises & 200+ financial institutions.

That creates a three sided network where merchants provide transaction distribution, brands bring offers & consumer engagement, while banks provide credit & financial products.

The Issuing & Acquiring platform is an important monetisation layer. Pine Labs Prepaid helps brands create gift cards, wallets, refunds, loyalty currencies etc. The business processed more than 64,000 Cr of GTV in FY26.

International expansion is another important medium term growth driver. International REV has compounded at 44% over the last 3 years & now contributes around 15% of total REV compared with 9% three years ago, with Pine Labs present across 22 countries. Management's objective is not simply to export the Indian POS product but to export the entire payments + affordability + issuing + fintech infrastructure stack.

The growth strategy therefore has three increasingly valuable profit pools.

The first is Payments Infrastructure - merchant acquiring, checkout, processing & settlement. This provides scale, recurring transactions & distribution.

The second is Brand & Consumer - affordability, prepaid, credit distribution, loyalty & consumer engagement. This allows Pine Labs to capture more economics around each transaction.

The third is Business Services, Data & AI - analytics, fraud, underwriting, identity, merchant intelligence & agentic commerce. Management highlights that industry profit pools are shifting from pure transaction processing towards higher value software, intelligence & automation.

If Pine Labs can sustain 20%+ REV growth (which is what the management is essentially guiding for) while continuing to shift mix towards higher margin products, operating leverage will continue to play out

Overall, Pine Labs is evolving from a payment acceptance company into a commerce infrastructure platform

I don’t need an analyst to tell me why a stock is cheap at 10x P/E.

I need them to tell me why it won’t remain cheap.

A low valuation by itself is not a thesis.

Many stocks stay cheap for years.

The important questions are:
- Is there a structural change in the business?
- Can earnings growth accelerate?
- What changes over the next 2-3 years?

And most importantly - why should the market value the company differently in the future?

Cheap valuations creates an opportunity only when there is a catalyst for change.

A low P/E can tell us that a stock looks inexpensive.

The more important question is what can change for that valuation to re-rate over time.

items.description_html:
So many IPOs come with huge subscriptions, strong GMPs, good listing gains & a lot of hype.

Valuations are often lofty, but in the excitement, investors tend to ignore the price they are paying.

History gives an interesting reminder.

A study of 377 Indian IPOs from 2005-15 found that only 38, or ~10%, outperformed the benchmark over the following 3 years.

Some recent popular examples make the point even clearer:
- FirstCry - IPO ₹465 - down ~58%
- Ola Electric - IPO ₹76 - down ~50%
- Swiggy - IPO ₹390 - down ~28%
- Cello World - IPO ₹648 - down ~44%
- Vikram Solar - IPO ₹332 - down ~48%
- Oswal Pumps - IPO ₹614 - down ~51%
And there are many such examples.

A strong listing doesn't necessarily mean a great long term investment.

Don't get caught in the IPO hype.

items.title: SEBI's latest F&O study has some very interesting data. During FY22-24, individual traders incurred aggregate net losses of more than ₹1.8 lakh Cr, w...
items.description_html:
SEBI's latest F&O study has some very interesting data.

During FY22-24, individual traders incurred aggregate net losses of more than ₹1.8 lakh Cr, with around 93% of traders losing money after transaction costs.

Among first time traders entering in FY25, 44% were still trading one year later.

For older cohorts, retention falls to 35-38% after 4-6 years & 27% after 10 years.

Experience did not improve trading outcomes

Loss makers increased from 91% among traders with 1 year of participation to 94% after 2 years, 96% after 3 years & 97% after 4 years.

Even after 5 consecutive years, 95% were cumulatively loss making.

Simply staying in F&O markets for longer did not translate into better outcomes.

Among traders who had already lost money in each of the previous two years & continued trading:
- 92% lost again in FY24
- 92% lost again in FY25
- 90% lost again in FY26

So roughly 9 out of 10 repeated loss makers continued to lose in the following year as well.

Among traders who remained active throughout FY22-26, only 0.5% were profitable in every single year. In comparison, around 66% lost money in all five years.

More trading generally meant worse outcomes.

Traders active for more than 100 days accounted for around 42% of traders but generated 94% of turnover & 87% of total losses.

items.description_html:
RT Nitin Sarin
Summary of what happened in the SpiceJet insolvency petitions today. Petitions A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H were argued, judgment reserved by the Court and set for pronouncement today. Pronouncement means the Hon'ble judges would give their verdict on whether to admit SpiceJet into insolvency (board would be dismissed, etc. etc) or to dismiss the applications of A to H outright. When the matters came up for pronouncement (not hearing) - Party A and SpiceJet said that they had entered into a settlement agreement and certain monies had been paid. The Court got livid as it had spent time and effort writing judgment. Parties B, C, D, E, F, G and H got up and objected saying there was no settlement in their matters and hence judgment may be passed. Clearly peeved, the Court has separated case A from the rest and ordered that pronouncement shall be day after tomorrow, i.e. 19th August, 2026. It was made clear that no further deferral would be made in any circumstance.

items.title: RT Sonal Varma: Beyond the headlines, AI has added jobs in Asia—so far. Our research finds 131,000 documented AI-related hires, compared with 61,000 ...
items.description_html:
RT Sonal Varma
Beyond the headlines, AI has added jobs in Asia—so far.

Our research finds 131,000 documented AI-related hires, compared with 61,000 job losses. But the headline numbers conceal an increasingly uneven impact:

• Job losses are concentrated in financial services and routine, lower-skilled technology roles.

• More than 90% of new jobs are in the technology sector, particularly AI training, data annotation and data operations.

• AI is creating a K-shaped labour market: entry-level hiring is weakening, while demand for experienced talent is rising.

• India is ground zero for this disruption because of its large IT and back-office sector. The net impact has been positive so far, but reduced campus recruitment represents a less visible form of displacement. @Nomura

items.title: Moderna is up ~100% premarket after melanoma vaccine trial success. Short explainer on why stock moved 100%+ rather than 20% The vaccine is not a prev...
items.description_html:
Moderna is up ~100% premarket after melanoma vaccine trial success. Short explainer on why stock moved 100%+ rather than 20%

The vaccine is not a preventive vaccine like a COVID shot. It's made after patient already has cancer. Each dose is built individually for that patient from the mutations found in their own tumour — you sequence the tumour, find the mutated proteins unique to it ("neoantigens"), and make an mRNA shot that teaches the immune system to hunt cells carrying those specific mutations.

It's the first proof the idea works. Neoantigen vaccines have been a theoretical hope in oncology for years, but this is the first randomised Phase 3 trial designed to definitively prove the benefit.

If the mechanism is real, it's platform technology — the same pipeline could in principle be pointed at lung, kidney, bladder cancers. One analyst noted the results also read positively for the vaccine's ongoing studies in other cancer types. That optionality is what "holy grail" headlines are reaching for.

items.title: RT Exencial Research Partners: Supply Chain stages for rare earth element magnets GEOGRAPHIC FRAGMENTATION OF THE VALUE CHAIN: NO COUNTRY DOMINATES EV...
items.description_html:
RT Exencial Research Partners
Supply Chain stages for rare earth element magnets

GEOGRAPHIC FRAGMENTATION OF THE VALUE CHAIN: NO COUNTRY DOMINATES EVERY LINK

China dominates reserves (34% of global REO-equivalent content), mining (~62% of global output) and, most decisively, refining/separation (91%) and NdFeB magnet manufacturing (92-94%).

Japan's advantage sits almost entirely downstream - in alloy technology and sintered magnet know-how where it holds roughly 6-7% of global magnet capacity but a disproportionate share of automotive-grade process expertise.

India, by contrast, ranks meaningfully only in reserves (world's 3rd or 4th largest, depending on classification) and has negligible mining, ~1% of global refining capacity, and zero commercial magnet manufacturing prior to the current scheme.

items.description_html:
Why did @RBI close the FCNR(B) window?
Here's what Governor @GovSMalhotra tells @FinancialXpress
On August 5, you said there was no proposal to close the FCNR(B) swap window prematurely. Nine days later, the RBI advanced the deadline by a month. What changed so materially during those nine days?
Advancing the last day of the swap window for FCNR(B) deposits is a well-thought-out, calibrated, prudent and data-driven response to the evolving situation. The second thing I would mention is that it is from a position of strength. From all three schemes put together, we expect inflows of at least $80 billion. This reflects the strong macroeconomic fundamentals of our country and would also further strengthen our balance of payments.

items.title: RT Gavin Baker: More data than open-source AI is taking share from OpenAI and Anthropic. Open source has gone from 28% token share to 62% token share ...
items.description_html:
RT Gavin Baker
More data than open-source AI is taking share from OpenAI and Anthropic. Open source has gone from 28% token share to 62% token share @vercel over the last 2 months. Chart from @rauchg

Super impressive given that the sum of OpenAI and Anthropic accelerated in July. So net token/AI infra demand accelerated even more than the acceleration we saw at the frontier. And suspect Grok growing even faster than open-source and we saw some of this in the @tryramp data.

Open-source AI taking share is positive for AI infrastructure demand as it lowers margins at the model layer and an open-source token costs just as much compute to produce as a frontier token. Nothing about open-source AI inference is “free.”

Most likely end state IMO is that closed, frontier tokens are 60-90% of economic value but only 15 to 25% of tokens.

items.title: RT Sonal Varma: Beyond the headlines, AI has added jobs in Asia—so far. Our research finds 131,000 documented AI-related hires, compared with 61,000 ...
items.description_html:
RT Sonal Varma
Beyond the headlines, AI has added jobs in Asia—so far.

Our research finds 131,000 documented AI-related hires, compared with 61,000 job losses. But the headline numbers conceal an increasingly uneven impact:

• Job losses are concentrated in financial services and routine, lower-skilled technology roles.

• More than 90% of new jobs are in the technology sector, particularly AI training, data annotation and data operations.

• AI is creating a K-shaped labour market: entry-level hiring is weakening, while demand for experienced talent is rising.

• India is ground zero for this disruption because of its large IT and back-office sector. The net impact has been positive so far, but reduced campus recruitment represents a less visible form of displacement. @Nomura

https://www.nomuraconnects.com/focused-thinking-posts/beyond-the-headlines-ai-has-added-jobs-in-asia-so-far/

items.title: Looks like the way boards of Indian internet companies reward founders and CEOs is changing. Earlier, boards of Indian internet companies rewarded fou...
items.description_html:
Looks like the way boards of Indian internet companies reward founders and CEOs is changing.

Earlier, boards of Indian internet companies rewarded founders and CEOs with ESOPs.

Now, as these companies have started generating cash, that could shift towards profit-sharing. This is probably one of the first examples among listed unicorns.

This pay revision also comes after Vijay Shekhar Sharma lost a large chunk of his ESOPs.

Last year, Paytm cancelled 2.1 crore stock options granted to Sharma in 2021 after SEBI questioned his eligibility for the grant, given his promoter status.

The options had a nominal exercise price and were worth over Rs 3,000 crore at Paytm's current market price.

Several other founders of internet companies like Eternal's Deepinder Goyal, Swiggy's Sriharsha Majety and Policybazaar's Yashish Dahiya also received sizeable option grants in the run-up to their IPOs.

items.description_html:
VC investors cashed out close to Rs 800 crore from two recently listed companies on Friday.

Amagi: Accel and Avataar Venture Partners entities sold nearly Rs 600 crore of shares in block deals at Rs 560 a piece.

Accel's two vehicles sold Rs 305 crore, while Trudy Holdings and AVP I Fund sold another Rs 282 crore.

At this price, Accel India VI and Trudy (Avataar entity) are sitting on roughly a 5x return.

Shadowfax: Qualcomm Ventures sold Rs 65 crore worth of shares in the IPO at Rs 124 apiece, making about 5.1x on its acquisition cost.

It sold 1.3% stake on Friday for about Rs 184 crore at Rs 245 a share - making 10x returns.

Still has 1% stake, worth about Rs 150 crore - total returns expected at Rs 400 crore.
